SMTO-HTTP-0036 — This connection needs sign-in details before SMTO can use it

GUID: 9779c83a-6f7c-441d-8901-729230b63029
Slug: http-credentials-missing
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The saved connection is missing a password, key or other sign-in value, or the service asked for sign-in and none was given. SMTO can't use the service until those details are added.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and select the HTTP connection the task uses. That's where SMTO keeps this connection's sign-in details.
  2. Under Authentication, choose the sign-in type the service needs and fill in any empty fields, such as Username and Password, API key or Token. SMTO found that a sign-in value this service needs is missing.
  3. Save, then select Test connection. When it shows Authenticated, run the task again. The test confirms the service accepts the new details before the task uses them.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Reachable and Authenticated, and the task's request is accepted.

If it still fails

  • Ask the owner of the service account for the right sign-in details and add them in Parameter Store. Never paste passwords, keys or tokens into a task, chat message, screenshot or the details you share.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected HTTP connection profile lacks required authentication values, or an unauthenticated read received a supported Basic, Digest or Bearer 401 challenge.

What this means

  • The selected profile lacks required authentication values, or an unauthenticated read receives a supported Basic/Digest/Bearer 401 challenge. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The selected profile lacks required authentication values, or an unauthenticated read receives a supported Basic/Digest/Bearer 401 challenge.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish pre-dispatch missing fields from an observed unauthenticated challenge; inspect advertised value paths privately.

How to fix it

  • Populate the profile's required auth fields in Parameter Store (the HTTP connection's Authentication section), or switch the profile to the auth type the target advertises in its WWW-Authenticate challenge. Keep secrets in Parameter Store, never in task text or arguments.
  • Provide required values through the supported credential or Parameter Store flow. Do not paste secrets into task instructions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended authentication values resolve through the supported flow and the resource read is accepted.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
